title: Atelier Palette — Minimal Hub & Rail Scaffold for Console Navigation
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Goal: Design a lightweight, extensible navigation scaffold ("Atelier Palette") that lets teams surface per-workspace dashboards, rollout controls, and cost lenses while minimizing cognitive load and improving discoverability. This ticket captures hypotheses, prototype artifacts, engineering constraints, and review notes for the first milestone (side rail + compact hub + workspace context persistence).

Problem statement: Current Console navigation mixes global actions, project-level routes, and ephemeral debugging tools in a dense left rail. Customers have expressed confusion when switching workspaces (lost context), difficulty finding rollouts and cost breakdowns, and slow onboarding for platform teams who need compact, task-focused surfaces.

Scope:
- Design a compact left rail variant with an expandable micro-hub (palette) that surfaces: Dashboards, Rollouts, Model Routes, Cost Lenses, and Settings.
- Define workspace switch affordance that preserves route context where possible and provides graceful fallbacks.
- Produce high-fidelity prototype for usability testing and handoff assets for engineering (CSS tokens, motion specs, ARIA labels).

Constraints & trade-offs considered:
- Keep primary rail < 72px when collapsed to maximize canvas area for dashboards vs adding dense labels.
- Favor client-side route mapping for instant workspace switch feedback; add server-side canonical redirect for deep-link integrity (trade-off: more engineering coordination).
- Accessibility: ensure keyboard-first navigation and visible focus ring for the palette, and include skip-links for dashboard tiles.

Success metrics:
- 20% reduction in average time-to-find Rollouts from usability tests.
- 30% fewer accidental workspace switches (measured via telemetry) within 6 weeks of rollout.
- No regression to console SLO due to client-side routing changes (tracked by infra).

Deliverables:
- Annotated Figma file with component tokens and motion microcopy.
- Usability test script and results doc.
- Engineering handoff with CSS vars, storybook snippets, and route map.
- Rollout plan for staged release with A/B to measure discoverability and cost-lens usage.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Collapsed rail prototype exists and is keyboard operable.
2) Workspace switcher preserves current route when target workspace supports the route; otherwise shows contextual landing and clear affordance to go to canonical dashboard.
3) Rollouts and Cost Lenses accessible via two clicks maximum from any top-level page.
4) Accessibility audit results (automated + 1 manual pass) attached.
5) Engineering review signoff documenting client-side vs server-side routing responsibilities.
comments: 2025-11-13 - Low-fi sketches completed; opted for a split 'micro-hub' pattern vs full-width overlay after early PM feedback that overlays hide important dashboard context.
2025-11-18 - PM review (Arjun Patel): prefer preserving route state on workspace switch where feasible; asked to list incompatible routes that should fallback to workspace home.

2025-11-20 - Engineering feasibility (Infra sync): Client-side route preservation is fine, but requires server canonicalization for deep links; estimated 3 engineer-days for routing layer changes. Recorded in PR #4282.
2025-11-24 - Accessibility review (Sophie Lin): keyboard flow stable; requested ARIA labels for palette items and a clearer announcement when workspace switches occur. Added to acceptance criteria.
2025-11-29 - Usability test plan uploaded; recruiting 8 participants (mix of platform and product engineers). Prototype link pushed to scout testing channel.
2025-12-02 - Design critique with execs: requested stronger affordance for Rollouts entry and an in-context cost badge on dashboard cards. We've added an optional cost chip pattern to variant B.
2025-12-04 - Handoff ready: storybook snippets and CSS token sheet attached; awaiting engineering estimate for integration sprint (ENG-20134 requested).
next_steps: Finalize A/B prototypes (compact palette vs persistent mini-rail) by 2025-12-11.
Run first round of moderated usability tests 2025-12-15 — compile findings by 2025-12-22.
Coordinate routing changes with infra team and merge PR #4282; track ENG-20134 for implementation scheduling.
Prepare rollout dashboard queries to measure discoverability, workspace switch failure rate, and cost-lens engagement.
Plan staged rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with telemetry gates and rollback plan for regressions.
